correctness.rationale: The signed hyperboloid side-distance equation gives the exact intersection of adjacent inward-offset hypercycles. A hyperbolic right-triangle identity gives the exact half-edge footpoint length, hence the entire offset perimeter. Coarea integration from the collapsing incenter gives the CDF and density with correct support and normalization. Differentiating the exact CDF with respect to the continuous polygon-angle parameter establishes strict side-count ordering. The finite and limiting densities have a provably unique crossing, where the CDF gap evaluates to the exact total variation formula; Taylor expansion supplies its two asymptotic orders. The n=3 CDF matches the prior full law, and an independently derived hyperbolic polar-area integral, density-normalization checks, crossing checks, and TV integration passed 810 deterministic tests. Infinite statements rest on the geometric proof, not finite checks.

value.rationale: Nearest-boundary clearance is a natural geometric probability invariant of ideal polygons with finite area and infinite perimeter. The complete exact finite-n law is a motivated missing benchmark beyond the known ideal-triangle case, and strict stochastic ordering answers how adding regular ideal sides changes typical clearance. The limit exhibits a nonobvious finite stochastic distribution even while inradius diverges, with a sharp computable total-variation convergence error of order 2/n and explicit second term. These features are structural, not numerical increments or a rephrased low-order expansion.
